THE SENTENCE THAT CLOSES THIS FIELD PREDATES THE JVMHARN-001 CLOSURE RECORDED ABOVE AND IS RETAINED UNCHANGED UNDER D6: when it was written the 27 were classified and none was fixed. As of 2026-08-23, 22 of the 27 are modelled by demangleValueClass in the harness and the residual is a PROJECTION of 5, not a measurement; the pin still publishes no coverage figure, and for the same reason it gave then -- the differential has not been re-run. The pin still publishes NO coverage figure: the 27 are now classified but not fixed, and a Kotlin coverage number read without JVMHARN-001 beside it would cover less than it appears to — the same rule AC-4 applies to a denominator.

entries.notes: Second Kotlin corpus pin (language-GA program G5, WP-J6): JetBrains' kotlinx.serialization, a reflectionless Kotlin-multiplatform serialization library (609 .kt + 6 .java at the pin; the 6 .java are module-info.java JPMS declarations, which carry no methods and produce no sites — expected). Tier 3 (nightly/manual, never the PR gate). Complements okio with a compiler-plugin-heavy, densely-generic Kotlin codebase for cross-language regression + JVM-binder breadth. Verified at pin time: graphi tables all 615 JVM files with ZERO parse or tabling crashes and the declared-type binder resolves 3517 typed Kotlin sites. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 (W1.b / SW-175), and the old sentence is kept above rather than overwritten because of what was wrong with it: 3517 is a NUMERATOR WITHOUT A DENOMINATOR — it says how many sites bound, never out of how many exist, which is the defect independent-review R6 named when it dropped Kotlin's recall threshold. The measured answer, same pin, same sha: the call-site binding rate is 19.16% = 2949 bound call sites / 15388 CST call sites (denominator counted by an INDEPENDENT tree-sitter walk, never from the binder), published with the full ten-reason skip histogram and every named exclusion in docs/rc/jvm-binding-rate.md. READ IT WITH ITS PARSE CAVEAT: the embedded tree-sitter Kotlin grammar leaves ERROR nodes in 80 of this pin's 609 .kt files (13.1%), so a recovered file still contributes a full denominator while the binder can no longer walk its bodies — guava's java equivalent is 0 of 621. The bias DIRECTION is measured and is anti-flattering: dirty parses DEPRESS the rate. Over the 529 cleanly-parsed files the rate is 21.15% (2908/13748); over the 80 dirty ones it is 2.50% (41/1640). An earlier version of this note said the direction was 'undetermined'; that was an incomplete measurement presented as an unavailable one and is retracted. SECOND FINDING: today's binder produces 3433 typed sites here (2949 call + 484 value), 84 FEWER than 3517, so the old numerator is not reproducible from this tree either — what it counted could not be determined, and the binder has changed since (ADR 0008 D6 corrected 2026-08-16 after JVMSOUND-001/002; SW-170 re-keyed the sweep). No attempt is made to reconcile the 84. Note the scope difference from the jvm_compile block above: the binding rate needs NO compiler and therefore covers ALL 615 files at the pin, not the 52 that compile. Compile coverage (SW-190, PARITY-COV-001 closure): 52 of 52 staged sources compile — coverage 1.0000 — measured 2026-08-21 against the post-SW-188 candidate. The 27 of 351 unbacked calls (the JVMHARN-001 value-class shape, recorded above) are a separate counterexample count, NOT bound to this figure: the figure answers 'does the source set compile', the unbacked calls answer 'does the binder's output agree with the bytecode'. entries.name: sql-abstention
entries.no_pin_reason: No representative open-source SQL corpus at the pin tier (SW-196 AC-2 honest abstention + ADR-W1 over-claim documentation). SQL has no canonical open-source corpus: SQL is not an import-driven language — its cross-file construct is JOIN / VIEW, not import — and the corpus's per-language model assumes a parser with a per-file CST plus cross-file references that resolve to an anchor node (the file/function model). A SQL project would consist of CREATE TABLE / CREATE VIEW / INSERT / SELECT with the file-level units being queries; the resolver's cross-file model does not cover this shape. ADR-W1 documents the over-claim that the SW-184 scaffold's audit named SQL at the cross-file-heuristic tier; SW-196 publishes the gap, files the G5 row as UNKNOWN, and does not substitute a low-quality pin (e.g. psql's own regression tests — too narrow; MySQL's server repo — not a SQL corpus; sqlfluff — a tool, not a SQL corpus).

entries.name: tier1-fixture-hero-yaml
entries.notes: Tier-1 pinned multi-file YAML fixture for the SW-202 hero-yaml tasks. YAML is graded intra-file-only. Per docs/rc/parity-classes-yaml.yaml's §5.5 paragraph the YAML 1.2 specification's TAG mechanism is the language-level hook an `!include ./other.yaml` node rides on, with two limits stated rather than overclaimed (YAML does not standardise !include itself, and anchors/aliases are stream-local). pipeline/build.yaml therefore writes BOTH shapes — `shared: !include ../shared/common.yaml` (the tag mechanism) and `include: ../shared/common.yaml` (the Ansible/Compose convention YAML gives no meaning) — so the two are distinguishable in the source. graphi resolves no tag, and the scenarios record that as honest-empty. The hero-yaml gate (cmd/eval/hero_yaml_test.go) asserts the 12 stable ops at the heuristic tier. No network.
